text:
Rasmus Andersson came to Vegas as a top-pair right shot, and 24 games in, the Calgary press is already writing about it: Daily Hive's headline on Nov. 16 called it "continuing to struggle with Golden Knights." He has 7 points and no power-play points while playing almost 20 minutes a night, well below the 47-point season he had last year.

Some of that is bad luck. With Andersson on the ice, Vegas has scored 12.1 fewer goals than its chances deserved, which has cost him points that usually come back. His shooting is exactly league average for a defenseman.

The part that isn't luck: the Golden Knights get fewer shot attempts than they allow with him on at five on five, and he rates about six points of expected-goal share below his teammates. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among defensemen last season, most of it from even-strength offense, so the ceiling is real. His ice time has gone up over the last ten games while Vegas lost four straight, which says Ryan Craig still trusts him. The goal against Nashville on Nov. 13 was a start.
headline: Andersson's slow start in Vegas
